Construct an AOF medial-axis representation

Source: R/mat.R
compute_mat.Rd

Uses the MLV signed-distance construction and a 60-sample average outward flux. The defaults are the package methods: a pixel-centred, tie-invariant flux (`aof="centered"`), a topology-preserving thinning that leaves no removable (simple) non-end pixel (`morphology="minimal"`) and order-invariant branch handling (`branch_rule="invariant"`). The published-compatible recipe is `aof="mlv2023", morphology="hmt8", branch_rule="mlv2023"`, with `threshold_angle = asin(0.3*pi/2)*180/pi` (28.11 degrees, flux threshold 0.3) to match the lab's datasets, which `computeAllMATfromVecLD` produced with the omitted-threshold value 0.3 (MLV-M004; the default 28 degrees gives 0.2989). The first two reproduce the published MATLAB MAT fields (distance map, AOF and skeleton) exactly on the Forest_DBW reference, and all three together reproduce the published per-pixel scores. `morphology="pratt"` is the Octave image backend. Empty ink sets have Inf distances and no skeleton; an all-ink image has no valid medial axis under this contour-background definition. Isolated ink pixels retain signed distance -1. The `"mlv2023"` flux uses the lowest R linear index among equidistant nearest boundary pixels, as MATLAB bwdist does.

Usage

compute_mat(
  mask,
  threshold_angle = 28,
  samples = 60L,
  epsilon = 1,
  min_component = NULL,
  min_branch_points = 10L,
  trace_branches = TRUE,
  spec = NULL,
  aof = c("centered", "mlv2023"),
  morphology = c("minimal", "hmt8", "pratt"),
  branch_rule = c("invariant", "mlv2023")
)

Arguments

mask

Binary matrix, TRUE for ink; or a drawing.

threshold_angle

Object angle in degrees, in [0,90].

samples, epsilon

AOF sampling parameters. Angles use alpha=(2*pi)/samples followed by alpha*k; the order matters when samples are mapped to discrete grid cells. With `aof="centered"`, samples must be a multiple of 4 (the sample directions must be closed under quarter turns and the diagonal reflection).

min_component

Minimum component size; default scales with image size.

min_branch_points

Spur length threshold, in pixels (default `branch_rule`) or Euclidean length (`"mlv2023"`). Under `"invariant"` only spurs (paths from an end pixel to a junction) shorter than this are pruned, shortest first with tied spurs kept together, and never a component's last path; see [trace_skeleton()].

trace_branches

Trace branches now; FALSE defers this work until scoring.

spec

Optional feature specification for raster and MAT settings.

aof

Flux sampling. `"centered"` (default) centres the sampling circle on the pixel, reads the nearest pixel cell (both cells for a point on a cell boundary) and averages unit directions over all equidistant nearest boundary pixels; it is independent of tie order and, for samples divisible by 4, the flux field of a given ink raster is equivariant under the eight lattice rotations/reflections. Pixels whose sampling circle leaves the image are set to 0 symmetrically on all four borders. `"mlv2023"` reproduces MATLAB computeAOF.m exactly, including lowest-index tie labels: its circle is centred on the pixel corner (i+0.5,j+0.5) while labels are read from `floor()` cells, which misplaces medial ridges by half a pixel and breaks that equivariance.

morphology

Thinning used for both ink and flux skeletons; see [skeletonize()]. `"minimal"` (default; no simple pixel with two or more neighbours remains, 2x2 blocks only where all four pixels are non-simple), `"hmt8"` (MATLAB-exact on the reference; may keep simple non-end pixels and removable 2x2 blocks) or `"pratt"`.

branch_rule

Branch tracing, scoring direction and contour mapping. `"invariant"` (default): pixel-graph tracing without repeated points and order-free spur pruning that keeps every skeleton component of two or more pixels (see [trace_skeleton()]), branch scores NA where undefined (branch ends before smoothing, branches too short for a property) instead of the published zeros and averaged over both traversal directions, tangent samples carrying the mean defined score of their segment's two points, the maximum over exact nearest-sample ties and over branches, and valid zeros retained; an isolated closed loop (no end or junction pixel) is scored with circular windows for local estimators (it has no start) and, for the mlv2023 mirror fit (a global greedy segmentation), as the mean over every start pixel and both directions; traced branches and per-pixel scores are unchanged by branch reversal, branch or contour renumbering, the traced start pixel (including that of an isolated closed loop), and lattice rotations/reflections of the MAT fields. The whole pipeline from a drawing is not guaranteed lattice-equivariant: thinning is sequential (direction-ordered) and the rasterizer resolves exact half-pixel ties by slope sign. `"mlv2023"`: the published chain (Kovesi edgelink/cleanedgelist tracing with duplicated merge points, forward scores, MLV fitLineSegments for mirror, last-writer skeleton rating image, MATLAB tangent enumeration order with lowest-index ties, zeros treated as missing). Together with `aof="mlv2023"` and `morphology="hmt8"` (the published-compatible recipe) this reproduces published MLV per-pixel scores.

Value

An `mlv_mat` with distance_map, nearest_boundary, AOF, skeleton, branches, mask and method parameters.
